text:
rachel: Heads-up — ACME Retail submitted a dedicated capacity ask in the intake form. They want a dedicated pool for embeddings + chat for an upcoming seasonal campaign. Key asks: 1) handle steady embeddings load ~2k qps, 2) support up to 120 concurrent low-latency chat streams, 3) daily burst up to 3x for 3 hours, 4) 99.9% availability SLA, and 5) pricing estimate for reserved + burst. Can product/infra give a sizing + rollout recommendation?

anya: thanks for pulling in. couple clarifying q's: which model families do they want for embeddings/chat (open models or want Redwood-managed variants)? what's target p50/p95 latency for chat? and prefix lengths for chat context?

rachel: sales notes: they want high-quality open LLMs we host (similar to gpt-like family) and would accept a quantized variant if we recommend. Target p95 chat latency ~300ms token, p50 ~100ms. Typical context ~512 tokens, average response 80 tokens. Embeddings: batchable requests, p95 <= 200ms.

dan: quick back-of-envelope for capacity: chat workload ~120 concurrent streams * 80 tokens/resp * (p50 token rate) — rough GPU needs depend on model/quantization. For a mid-size open chat model on H100 we estimate ~12-16 streams per GPU at our optimized runtime. So ballpark 8-10 GPUs for chat baseline. Embeddings: 2k qps batchable — if we batch to 64 and use quantized encoder we can get ~2k qps on 2-3 GPUs. Burst 3x headroom -> add burst pool or autoscale policy to allow 3x for short window -> need extra 18-30 GPUs hot if we rely on immediate scale, or use queued burst with degraded latency.

mike: +1 to defining burst strategy now. We shouldn't promise instant 3x without a burst pricing and capacity reservation. Two options: 1) reserved baseline (10 GPUs) + pre-warmed burst pool (additional 20 GPUs reserved but off until needed) OR 2) baseline reserved + cloud elastic burst with warm-up and fallback to smaller model / increased latency.

patrick: customer asked for committed pricing for baseline and one-off burst credit. They prefer a predictable monthly commit and pay-as-you-go for burst hours. Need numbers we can attach to the commercial term sheet by EOD Fri.

linda: for launch criteria we need: (a) validated perf on customer prompts (we'll run 10k sample evals), (b) infra can sustain p95 SLA under their traffic pattern in staging, (c) documented fallback policy (model variant or queue), (d) price approved by finance.

anya: next steps from product: 1) run a small perf matrix (chat model variants + quantization) with their sample corpus, 2) provide two recommended architectures: reserved+prewarm and reserved+elastic-burst with fallback, each with cost estimate and SLA tradeoffs, 3) draft rollout plan with canary and immediate rollback triggers.

ops-bot: provisioning ETA: if we reserve additional GPUs we can schedule capacity in ~7 business days once PO hits. Elastic cloud burst via partner clouds ~48-72 hours to enable autoscale policies.

rachel: dan/linda/anya — can you run the perf matrix today/tomorrow? sales needs baseline cost ranges for Patrick. I'll collect their sample payloads.

dan: I'll run a quick cluster perf job for chat variants today. embedding microbenchmarks tomorrow AM. I'll post raw numbers here.

linda: I'll own the rollout checklist and can set the SLO tests in staging once dan posts numbers.

anya: I'll draft two architecture options and include launch criteria. Will also propose quantization recommendations and expected quality delta.

patrick: thanks team. I'll tell ACME we're working on two options and will follow up with pricing by Friday. Please tag me on the final cost sheet. :thumbsup:

salesbot: Created ticket RED-5492 for ACME dedicated intake and attached initial intake form: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-5492

rachel: perfect. if perf looks good and ops can prewarm, recommendation likely reserved baseline (10 GPUs) + pre-warmed burst pool (20 GPUs) + canary rollout. If we can't prewarm cost-effectively, recommend reserved baseline + elastic burst with fallback to smaller model. I'll update ACME after we validate numbers. :white_check_mark:
